newsitem.title: UK: Britain has driest start to year since 1929.
newsitem.headline: Britain has driest start to year since 1929.

text.p: Rain in the past few days has failed to put a damper on the driest start to the year in England and Wales since 1929, the Meteorological Office said on Wednesday.

According to provisional figures, 152 mm of rain fell across England and Wales during the first four months of this year, while in the same period of 1929, there was only 124 mm. The comparable figure for last year was 245.5 mm.

The Met Office said it had been the driest April since 1984. With a day to go, gauges in England and Wales had collected 25mm of rain this month, which is 42 percent of the long term average for April of 60 mm.
Rainfall in April 1996 was 48.3 mm, or 80.5 percent of the long term average, while in April 1984, there were only 11 mm of rain.

The mean central England temperature in April was 8.9 C, 1.0 C above the long term average 7.9 C. There was an average of 5.47 hours of sunshine each day during the month, which is 112 percent of the long term average of 4.88 hours a day.
The forecast for May is for more changeable weather. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
